messages:
maria: alerting — SFO GPU fabric showing sustained packet drops and multiple provisioning controller failures allocating new GPU pods. tagging @kevin-sre @aj for immediate triage and traffic plan
ops-bot: automated alert: region=sfo cluster=gpu-pool-1 metric=packet_loss pct=12.7 window=5m severity=high
kevin-sre: joining. I see tor-12 counters climbing, SNIC flapping. Rebooted a couple blades, conn resets persist. Suspect network fabric microbursts causing kernel queue drops rather than OOMs
aj: impact surface? only provisioning or are live inference requests affected too?
kevin-sre: provisioning is queuing; live pods showing transient 5-10x tail latency for heavy KV access paths. Most sessions OK but error rate spikes on large-model KV hits. Avoid evictions for now
sarah-support: prepping status page blurb — need an ETA and what remediation we are doing so I can be explicit to customers
leo-plat: propose staged regional steer to eu-west1: start 30% -> monitor 10m -> 70% -> evaluate full cutover. Use tiered-smart-router policy to minimize cold-start surge
kevin-sre: plan outline: 1) mark sfo degraded in routing 2) steer traffic primary->eu-west1 fallback->us-west2 3) pause new provisioning to sfo 4) monitor for 30m and iterate
kevin-sre: routing policy example (infra-control):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/routing/policies/steer -d '{"region_order":["eu-west1","us-west2","sfo"], "weights":{"eu-west1":30,"sfo":70}}' -H \"Authorization: Bearer $INFA_API\"
```
aj: heads-up on cost: cross-region egress + extra model loads will bump egress/token costs. Ballpark +18-25% while steer at this level
sarah-support: draft statuspage copy:
```
We are investigating degraded GPU provisioning and intermittent networking errors in SFO. We are proactively steering traffic to eu-west1 to reduce impact. Some requests may experience increased latency or additional cost. ETA for mitigation: 30-60 minutes. Updates every ~10 minutes.
```
kevin-sre: kicking off staged steer (30% to eu-west1) now
devops-automation-bot: job=traffic-steer user=kevin-sre status=started job_id=ts-2143689922-1
maria: tagging @sales-contacts — please notify enterprise customers with dedicated pools. We may need manual migrations or to pause non-critical provisioning to preserve capacity
devops-automation-bot: monitor=latency-metrics job=ts-2143689922-1 threshold=95pctl alert_if_increase>2x
kevin-sre: t+8m metrics: eu-west1 ingestion stable. sfo provision queue down ~40%. tail latency improved 2.1s -> 1.1s on impacted routes
leo-plat: ramp to 70% now. watch for cache misses / model cold loads
kevin-sre: applying next patch:
```
kubectl patch routepolicy steer-policy -p '{"weights":{"eu-west1":70,"sfo":30}}' --type=merge
```
devops-automation-bot: job=traffic-steer user=kevin-sre status=running job_id=ts-2143689922-2
sarah-support: updated status page: ETA narrowed to 30-45m; added note about potential cost impact and support contact link
maria: ops action item — keep list of dedicated customers for manual migration approvals. tag me for sign-off
kevin-sre: t+22m: traffic at eu-west1=70%. Errors down ~88% from peak. Provision backlog cleared to baseline. tor-12 still shows intermittent resets; vendor scheduled rack-level maintenance 02:00 UTC
oncall-bot: incident logged: INC-2026-2143689922 severity=high owner=kevin-sre
sarah-support: posting customer update: mitigation steps, timeline, vendor ETA (02:00 UTC), brief cost advisory and support link
maria: closing loop for now — failover executed smoothly, no P0/P1 escalations beyond info requests. Follow-ups: postmortem + cost-reconciliation ticket P50-2143689922
kevin-sre: filing initial RCA notes and vendor ticket id. Recommend tuning automated fallback to go 0->30->70 within ~10m next time and adding a dry-run cost calculator for steers
sarah-support: will attach status page snapshots and outbound comms to the incident ticket
maria: thanks team :thumbsup:
